trailheadDirection: From Interstate 90 exit 52, turn onto State Route 906 and follow Erste Strasse (Alpental Access Road) for 1.1 miles to the Alpental parking lot just below the main lodges. A Northwest Forest Pass is needed to park.
approach: From the Alpental parking lot, pick up the Snow Lakes climbers trail and follow it north for about 2 miles to the south side of the mountain, where the base of the climb is.
note: Area page gives lot and walk; ski area page gives the drive.

trailheadDirection: From Interstate 90 exit 52, turn onto State Route 906 and follow Erste Strasse (Alpental Access Road) for 1.1 miles to the Alpental parking lot just below the main lodges.
approach: From the Alpental main parking lot, the base of the Practice Wall is 1,000 ft east-northeast of the lot. You can also follow the drainage running north-northeast from between the two Snoqualmie Pass Hideaways buildings. The walk takes about 15 minutes, or 45 to 60 minutes through deep snow.
note: Route page location text plus ski area directions.

trailhead: Frenchman Coulee parking on Vantage Road
trailheadDirection: From Seattle take Interstate 90 east across the Columbia River past Vantage to exit 143, turn left onto Silica Road, go under the highway and take the first left onto Vantage Road. Drive 1.4 miles down the canyon to parking on the left. The area page posts an access warning for May 2026: the area is effectively closed because of problems with the main road in.
approach: From the Frenchman Coulee parking on Vantage Road, the falls can be reached from below via the Sunshine Wall, or from above by heading south-southeast from the lot.
note: Crag page is thin; drive from parent Frenchman Coulee page. Notes May 2026 closure warning.

trailheadDirection: From Leavenworth, drive Icicle Creek Road, reached from US-2, for about 6.5 miles; the pullout is on the right.
approach: From the Icicle Buttress pullout, the crag rises right beside the road, so the base is a short walk up from the pullout.
note: Three area pages agree on pullout on the right at 6.4-6.5 miles up Icicle Road.

trailheadDirection: In Spokane, drive to Canyon Drive and use the upper of the two parking lots.
approach: From the Indian Canyon upper parking lot, follow the trail for less than a mile to the creek bed, where the short flow forms.
note: One area page; no driving beyond Canyon Drive.

trailhead: Tinkham Road turnaround by the highway maintenance facility
trailheadDirection: From Interstate 90 take exit 42 for Tinkham Road and drive a short distance southwest. In summer the McClellan Butte trailhead can be reached; in winter park at the turnaround next to the highway maintenance facility.
approach: From the Tinkham Road turnaround by the highway maintenance facility, head for the north and northeast side of the butte, where the snow couloir is. The full trip is about 7 miles round trip with over 3000 ft of climbing.
note: Area and route pages; walk-in to the couloir base is not described in detail.

trailheadDirection: From Interstate 90 exit 52, turn onto State Route 906 and follow Erste Strasse (Alpental Access Road) for 1.1 miles to the Alpental parking lot just below the main lodges. The walk starts from the upper lot above the base area.
approach: From the Alpental upper parking lot, follow the well-traveled trail to the small lake in the basin on the east side of Bryant Peak. The ice forms on the cliffs around the northwest side of the lake.
note: Area page for walk; ski area page for drive. Upper lot location is inferred from the area page only.

trailheadDirection: From Interstate 90 exit 52, turn onto State Route 906 and follow Erste Strasse (Alpental Access Road) for 1.1 miles to the Alpental parking lot just below the main lodges.
approach: From the Alpental parking lot, go up the slope on the left side of the Armstrong Express chair, then descend easy snow to the falls, which can be seen from the chair. The falls are inside the ski area boundary in winter.
note: Route page location text; parking inferred from the Armstrong chair being at Alpental.

trailheadDirection: From Leavenworth, drive Icicle Road for about 8.5 miles, turn left on Eightmile Road (Forest Road 7600), then stay right on Forest Road 7601 for about 4 miles to the trailhead. A day-use fee of $5 per vehicle applies, and Forest Road 7601 is closed to vehicles every winter.
approach: From the Stuart Lake trailhead, follow the Stuart Lake trail to the lake and go all the way to its west end. Continue through the trees about a quarter mile to an open field, where the ice lines are on the left below the north face of the mountain. If the winter gate at the start of Icicle Road is shut, the walk adds about 8 miles each way.
note: Area page for the walk, Forest Service page for the drive, fee and winter closure.

trailheadDirection: From the Mazama store, drive 1.5 miles northwest on Lost River Road to the large parking lot on the right. The lot is on private property used by climbers with permission.
approach: From the Fun Rocks parking lot, walk past Fun Rock and keep right on the Spokane Gulch trail toward Mazama. Continue past A-Wall to a large upper bench well above the valley floor. Where the trail turns right to head east, go straight north toward a stand of trees, and a faint path leads to the crag.
note: Crag page for the walk, parent page for lot and drive.

trailheadDirection: From South Canyon Road in Ellensburg, drive Umtanum Road about 10 miles southwest to the trailhead.
approach: From the Umtanum Creek Falls trailhead, walk alongside the creek to the falls, a drop in a forested gorge ringed by basalt columns.

trailheadDirection: From Enumclaw, drive State Route 410 toward Crystal Mountain; about 30 minutes out, a pullout sits on the right at the falls.
approach: From the Skookum Falls pullout, the river crossing is the hardest part of the approach, and how to cross changes from year to year; one party found an ice dam upstream.
note: Route page location text; area page agrees on SR 410 from Enumclaw.
crag: Waterfall ice and mixed routes in the SW Cascades
